title: Argument by Emotive Language
description: Substituting facts and evidence with words that stir up emotion, with the attempt to manipulate others into accepting the truth of the argument.
logical_form:
Person A claims that X is true.

Person A uses very powerful and emotive language in the claim.

Therefore, X is true.

examples.example: By *rejecting* God, you are rejecting goodness, kindness, and love itself.
examples.explanation: Instead of just “not believing” in God, we are  “rejecting” God, which is a much stronger term—especially when God is associated with “goodness.”

examples.example: The Bible is filled with stories of God's *magic*.
examples.explanation: Instead of using the more accepted term “miracles,” the word “magic” is used that connotes powers associated with fantasy and make-believe in an attempt to make the stories in the Bible seem foolish.

examples.example: I don’t see what’s wrong with engaging the services of a professional escort.
examples.explanation: That’s just a nice way of saying, “soliciting a hooker.”  No matter what you call it unless you live in certain parts of Nevada (or other parts of the world), it is still legally wrong (not necessarily morally wrong).

exceptions: Language is powerful and should be used to draw in emotions, but never at the expense of valid reasoning and evidence.
tips: : *Euphemisms*, when used correctly, reflect good social intelligence. When in a business meeting, say, “Pardon me for a moment, I have to use the restroom,” rather than “Pardon me for a moment, I have to move my bowels.”
references: Walton, D. (2006). *Fundamentals of Critical Argumentation*. Cambridge University Press.
description_et: Faktide ja tõendite asendamine emotsioone õhutavate sõnadega, katsega manipuleerida teisi väite tõesust aktsepteerima.
logical_form_et:
Isik A väidab, et X on tõsi.

Isik A kasutab väites väga võimsat ja emotsionaalset keelt.

Seetõttu on X tõene.
exceptions_et: Keel on võimas ja seda tuleks kasutada emotsioonide tõmbamiseks, kuid mitte kunagi kehtivate põhjenduste ja tõendite arvelt.
tips_et: : *Eufemismid* peegeldavad õigel kasutamisel head sotsiaalset intelligentsust. Kui ärikohtumisel öelge: "Vabandage korraks, ma pean tualetti kasutama", selle asemel, et "Vabandage korraks, ma pean oma soolestikku liigutama".

examples_et.example: Jumala *hülgamisega* lükkate tagasi headuse, lahkuse ja armastuse enda.
examples_et.explanation: Selle asemel, et lihtsalt "ei uskuda" Jumalasse, "tõrjume" Jumalat, mis on palju tugevam termin – eriti kui Jumal on seotud "headusega".
examples_et.original_example: By *rejecting* God, you are rejecting goodness, kindness, and love itself.
examples_et.original_explanation: Instead of just “not believing” in God, we are  “rejecting” God, which is a much stronger term—especially when God is associated with “goodness.”

examples_et.explanation: Selle asemel, et kasutada enam aktsepteeritud mõistet "imed", kasutatakse sõna "maagia", mis tähistab fantaasia ja teesklusega seotud võimeid, püüdes muuta Piibli lood rumalaks.
examples_et.original_example: The Bible is filled with stories of God's *magic*.
examples_et.original_explanation: Instead of using the more accepted term “miracles,” the word “magic” is used that connotes powers associated with fantasy and make-believe in an attempt to make the stories in the Bible seem foolish.

examples_et.example: Ma ei saa aru, mis viga on professionaalse saatja teenuste kasutamises.
examples_et.explanation: See on lihtsalt tore viis öelda: "Hakkuri otsimine".  Olenemata sellest, kuidas te seda nimetate, välja arvatud juhul, kui elate teatud Nevada osades (või mujal maailmas), on see ikkagi juriidiliselt vale (mitte tingimata moraalselt vale).
examples_et.original_example: I don’t see what’s wrong with engaging the services of a professional escort.
examples_et.original_explanation: That’s just a nice way of saying, “soliciting a hooker.”  No matter what you call it unless you live in certain parts of Nevada (or other parts of the world), it is still legally wrong (not necessarily morally wrong).
